entities.name: Otto V or III, Duke of Bavaria
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Otto III, a member of the Wittelsbach dynasty, was the Duke of Lower Bavaria from 1290 to 1312 and the King of Hungary and Croatia between 1305 and 1307. His reign in Hungary was contested by Charles Robert of the Angevin dynasty.

As Duke of Lower Bavaria, Otto III oversaw significant territorial expansion, including the incorporation of the Duchy of Carinthia and the Principality of Austria.

His reign as King of Hungary and Croatia was marked by power struggles with neighboring states, including the Kingdom of Bohemia and the Principality of Transylvania.

Otto III's legacy in Bavaria was cemented through his patronage of the arts and architecture, including the construction of the Wittelsbach Castle in Landshut.

Despite his disputed reign in Hungary, Otto III's impact on regional politics and diplomacy cannot be overstated.

The phrase 'Otto III, the 'Eternal King' of Hungary' was coined by 14th-century chroniclers to reflect his unyielding resolve in defending his territories against rival claimants.
